headline: Approved February minutes and reviewed updates on rain barrels, de-paving, Amelia Earhart Dam, and Green Malden Fair planning
summary: The Climate Action & Sustainability Commission discussed project updates including rain barrel distribution, a de-paving grant application, the Amelia Earhart Dam resolution, a Clean Energy Coach research project, and the Wicked Cool Mystic project. The commission approved the February minutes, planned logistics for the Green Malden Fair, reviewed working group progress on data collection and communications, tabled discussion of Household Hazardous Waste Days and future meeting invites, and set the next meeting for April 8 at 5:30 PM.
decisions: Approved the February minutes on a motion by Bob, seconded by Lipin.
Tabled the Household Hazardous Waste Days discussion for a future meeting.
Tabled discussion of future invites to CASC meetings for the next meeting.

Project Updates (5 min)
Rain barrel updates. (Amanda/Bekah)
 Bekah presented that we are considering using the Malden Farmer’s Market to distribute rain 
barrels
 Chris Rosa suggested using the Forestdale Cemetery storage as an alternate location for 
distribution. We do not currently know how many rain barrels. We also discussed Pine Banks for 
distribution.
 We plan to table at Green Malden Fair for sign ups, and distribute 1 month later (week before 
Memorial Day)
 Rachel raised that we could cap the number of barrels to limit the risk of leftover barrels.
 Rebekah and Amanda will speak with the barrel company to specify dates and numbers.
Minutes to be Approved (4 min)
Meeting now has quorum.
Bob moved to approve the minutes; Lipin seconded. CASC voting members approved the 
February minutes.
Additional Project Updates (10 min)
De-paving project updates. (Bekah)
 Selected site for application is the High School courtyard. The application is due next week.
 Rebekah and Auka will do outreach to Malden High School students and ask for a letter of 
support.
 Part of the funding will be for Malden-owned depaving tools that can be made available for 
Malden residents to do their own depaving projects.
Amelia Earhart Dam project updates. (Councilor McDonald)
 Rebekah sent the commission to the Mayor.
 Councilor McDonald read the drafted resolution for City Council that will be voted on in the 
March 24 meeting. 
 Bob asked if S.2542 amendment language has been submitted to committee yet; it currently is 
in ways & means.
Clean Energy Coach research updates. (Will/Julia)
 Julia and Will will start scheduling interviews next week, and then (ETA May 2026) write a 
recommendations memo for the City of Malden on how to run a coaching program. 
 Will described the CELT fellowship and the opportunity to coordinate with the Acton CELT 
fellow.

 Green Malden Fair – we can table and gather contact information for potential coaches and 
Malden residents who want to do more. We need to phrase this clearly so people know that the 
program is not ready yet. Will pointed at resources in the shared folders. Julia and Will to work 
on this ahead of the Green Malden Fair.
Wicked Cool Mystic project updates. (Bekah)
 This is a multi-phased project. Phase 1 is water bottle fillers. Phase 2 will be shade creation and 
the Skating Park. 
 We are applying for a 3rd phase, and discussed potential scope. Possible options include:
o Misting tents, water handouts. We talked about leveraging the Summer Youth program 
(mid-July to mid-August), but need to confirm how to reserve their time – difficult to 
schedule a weather-dependent work program in advance. 
o Additional bus shelter; this had been raised with Councilor Winslow
o Revisit alternate plans from Phase 2
o Chris Rosa had ideas from an older application involving planting, shading and green 
roofs. He will locate the older application.
o Benches in shaded areas.
 Malden may own existing misting tents that Chris Rosa’s summer team could use to do pop ups. 
Rebekah to check on how to access the tents.
